comment: The vectors binding cyfr-locus (apps/locus/keeper, Go) and its one client (apps/locus/lib/locus/keeper.ex, Elixir), which every Locus role spawns through (the runtime's worker service, the builds service and the backends service), through one codec (apps/prima/lib/prima/keeper_protocol.ex): the keeper accepts every valid request and refuses every invalid one with its code, every side encodes each frame to the bytes given, and the client understands every reply. `reserved_env_prefixes` are the variable name prefixes no spawn may carry in its `env`, CYFR's, Locus's and the keeper's own (its channel variable is KEEPER_CHANNEL): the keeper refuses them, and CYFR and the backends service refuse a backend definition that names one. `frames` are the stdio and attach streams every client carries; `control_frames` are the control stream (4) of a spawn that asked for a control channel with `control: true`, carrying Prima.RunnerControl lines (tests/fixtures/runner_control.json) verbatim between a worker service and its runner's fd 3, and a zero-length one ending the stream. The client refuses a control frame on a spawn that never asked for the channel. `relay_frames` are the relay stream (5) of a spawn of an isolated pool, carrying Prima.RunnerRelay frames (tests/fixtures/runner_relay.json) verbatim between a worker service and its runner's fd 4: the keeper sends nothing on it, its end frame included, until the client has sent on it first, and the client's first frame opens it, a zero-length one included, which ends nothing; after that a zero-length frame ends it. `relay_streams` pin that rule on the relay: a spawn whose client never opens the stream receives no stream-5 frame, and one whose client opens it receives what the command wrote to fd 4 and the stream's end. A spawn of any pool may carry `memory_bytes`, its memory bound, from 16777216 to 1099511627776: zero is not 'no bound', and a bound that is not a whole number of bytes in that range is refused. Every `exited` says in `memory` what the kernel killed processes of the spawn for, as the group's own counters say: `cap` for that bound, `machine` for a limit above it, `either` for a kill the counters cannot lay to one of the two, which is never called `cap`, null for no kill or for counters that could not be read. A place follows one piece of work from before its preparation to its release: the client mints its `id` and names its `kind` (`warm`, `run`, `build`, `program` or `terminal`) and, where it has them, its `athanor` and `subject`, the `athanor` of the grammar every Locus wire gives an athanor's id (Prima.RunnerControl: 1 to 256 printable ASCII characters, no space) and the `subject` of the id grammar, and the keeper answers `placed`, or refuses a place of an id it already holds as `bad_request`; a `drop` frees a place no spawn named and is not answered; an `assign` has an `id` of its own beside the `place` it names, gives that place another kind, athanor and subject, and is answered under that `id` alone, `assigned` once the keeper applied it, or refused `bad_request` where the keeper holds no such place; every `spawn` names its `place`, which no other spawn may name, and it is free at its spawn's `released`, which is the keeper's word alone: a spawn refused before the keeper made anything of it is refused under its `id` alone and frees its place at once, and one refused after the keeper made it (its command could not be run, say) is refused under its `id` and the `spawn_id` the keeper gave it, and gets one `released` under that `spawn_id` when its cleanup is done and its place freed. The keeper reads every spawn's group once a second. A `measure` has an `id` of its own beside the `place` it names and is answered under that `id` alone, as a home request is, from the last reading: `measured` with the place's `kind`, `athanor` and `subject` of the moment, the `bytes` of its spawn's group that cannot be given back (`anon + shmem + kernel - slab_reclaimable` from one read of its `memory.stat`, so never file cache), `lesser`, true where that kernel counts no `kernel` memory and `bytes` sums the parts it names, and `age_ms`, how old the reading is; or refused `unmeasured` where the keeper holds no such place or has no reading of it yet: no reading is ever sent as zero. Every spawn also carries `cpu_quota`, the microseconds of CPU time its group may use in every period of `request_bounds.cpu_period` (100000, so 100000 is one CPU), from `min_cpu_quota` to `max_cpu_quota`: zero, a missing one and one out of that range are refused, and the keeper writes it to the group's cpu.max before the command starts. `memory_unavailable` is the code for any bound a keeper cannot enforce, its memory or its CPU: such a keeper refuses every spawn so, and none runs unbounded. A spawn's `isolation` is `netns` or absent: the keeper names its isolated pools on its command line (`--pool runner:30101-30108:netns`), starts every spawn of one in a user and network namespace of its own that maps the pooled uid and gid to themselves, and refuses as `bad_request` a spawn of an isolated pool without `isolation` and one of any other pool with it, a decision of the pool it names and so not a vector here; the runner spawns carry it, and Locus's build and backends spawns, whose pools are not isolated, do not. `bounds` are the largest frame payload each side writes or reads and the longest request or reply line the keeper and its client accept, spelled once per side and pinned here. `reserved_env` are the variable names no spawn may carry in its `env`, `signals` the signals a `signal` request may name, `request_bounds` a request's ceilings (argv entries, env entries, the bytes of one value, of argv and env together and of an attach path, a release's grace, a spawn's memory bound, least and most, and a pseudo-terminal's rows and columns, `max_pty_size`) and `rlimits` each resource limit a spawn may lower, its least and its most, the most being the keeper's ceiling and the default of every spawn but a kept one, which takes no default for a limit `kept_unbounded_rlimits` names (its file size: its disk is held by its home's bound and the kept homes' volume) though it may still lower it: each side spells them once, and each side's suite holds its own to these. A spawn may also carry `home_mode` (`scratch`, today's home and the reading of its absence, or `kept`), a kept home's clean absolute `home_path`, its own `home_uid` and an optional `home_max_bytes`, which only a `kept` spawn carries, and `pty`, the size of a pseudo-terminal, an object of exactly `rows` and `cols`, each an integer from 1 to `request_bounds.max_pty_size`, whose absence means no pseudo-terminal (`true` and `false` are refused); `home_make`, `home_measure` and `home_retire` name a kept home by `path` and `uid`, and `request_bounds` holds their bounds too. Each of `home_requests` (a kept spawn, a spawn with a `pty` of 40 rows by 120 columns and the three home requests) is valid, while a spawn naming `scratch` and no `pty` is today's spawn. The keeper runs a kept spawn under its `home_uid` in its home at `home_path`, both its `--kept-homes <root>:<first>-<last>`'s (a home directly under the root, a uid of the range), and takes no uid of the pool for it; it refuses as `home_over_cap` a kept spawn whose home already holds `home_max_bytes`; it gives a `pty` spawn a pseudo-terminal of that size as its stdin, stdout and stderr, so its stdout frames carry the terminal and its stderr ends at once, and a `resize` (`spawn_id`, `rows` and `cols`, bounded as `pty`'s) sets the terminal's size, the kernel signalling SIGWINCH to its foreground process group, with no reply but a refusal like `signal`'s: `unknown_spawn` for a spawn the keeper does not hold and `bad_request` for one without a pseudo-terminal; and it answers `home_make` (the home made, 0700, by a helper running as the uid), `home_measure` (the bytes allocated under it) and `home_retire` (every process of the uid ended and the home removed) with `home_replies`, the last two of which are the `home_over_cap` refusal and the `uid_busy` one: a kept home's uid is retiring from the release of its last spawn until every process of the uid is ended and nothing it left outside its home remains, quarantined when that cannot finish, and the keeper refuses `home_make` and a kept spawn on a uid retiring, quarantined or live under another home as `uid_busy`, a kept spawn of the same home waiting for its retirement first. A member is judged by its presence, never by a zero value: no member is ever null, a spawn's `home_mode` or `isolation` that is present takes one of its values, the empty string not among them, and a member another type carries is refused on a request whatever its value, `false` and the empty string included. A spawn that is not isolated may carry `hosts`, 1 to `request_bounds.max_hosts` distinct exact hostnames (lowercase labels of letters, digits, hyphens and underscores; no wildcard, scheme, port or trailing dot; no address literal, IPv4 or IPv6, a name whose last label is all digits among them), the only hosts its command may reach beside the resolver and the deployment's private hosts; absent keeps the island's public-hosts rule. A keeper given `--guard` resolves them at the spawn and has the island's egress guard admit those addresses for the spawn's uid, or clear the uid for a spawn without them, before the command starts; it refuses a spawn one of whose hosts resolves to no address as `hosts_unresolved`, and one whose egress the guard does not confirm, or that names hosts to a keeper without a guard, as `guard_unavailable`, the last two of `replies`.

relay_frames.why: the client opens the stream: a zero-length first frame, which ends nothing
a runner relay frame carried verbatim: a host_answer, as tests/fixtures/runner_relay.json spells one
once the stream is open, a zero-length frame ends it

unused.why: a spawn of an isolated pool whose command writes a runner relay frame to fd 4 and exits, the client never sending on stream 5: the relay ends stdout, stderr and control and sends no stream-5 frame, its end frame included

opened.why: the same spawn with the client opening stream 5 by a zero-length frame: what the command wrote to fd 4 arrives on stream 5, and the stream ends with a zero-length frame once the command's end is closed
